articles.title: Svitolina stays in WTA Finals hunt after remarkable fightback sees off Muchova
articles.summary: Ukrainian wins 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 after eight-minute timeout. Andreeva beats Sabalenka 6-4, 6-0 to top Group B. Elina Svitolina staged a remarkable comeback to beat Karolina Muchova and remain in the hunt for the WTA Finals title.
body: The Ukrainian looked to be on her way out of Indian Wells when she was a set down and required an eight-minute medical timeout. But she recovered to win 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 and stay in with a chance of reaching the semi-finals.
Svitolina, who was demolished 6-4, 6-0 by Mirra Andreeva in her opening round-robin match, told Sky Sports: “It was not an easy task to do.
“I was pretty angry at myself, after the first match and after the first set also. Things didn’t go my way, so I tried to direct this anger towards the ball and found my game in the end.

“I think the level was back in the third set. I just tried to give it all in this match because I know I would be eliminated if I lost. So I just tried to really release all this energy and find these openings against Karolina. She’s such a tough opponent.

articles.title: Stephen Curry attacks treatment of women after former players criticize wife Ayesha’s movie kiss
articles.summary: Warriors star defends wife over romantic comedy role. Arenas called Ayesha ‘only blemish’ on Curry family. Four-time NBA champion condemns double standards. Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has criticized several ex-professional athletes for questioning his wife Ayesha’s decision to appear…
body: The four-time NBA champion posted a 90-second video on Instagram on Wednesday in response to comments by former NBA players Gilbert Arenas and Nick Young, as well as former NFL players Emmanuel Acho and LeSean McCoy, following the release of Ayesha Curry’s new film, Second Chance Holiday.

The romantic comedy, which premiered on the Roku Channel on 5 November, features Ayesha in her first leading film role opposite actor Matthew Daddario. A scene in which Ayesha Curry and Daddario kiss prompted criticism from several former athletes, who questioned her participation in the film and discussed its implications for her marriage.
Curry said the commentary had crossed a line by diminishing his wife’s professional achievements.
“I’ve been hearing a lot of noise, and usually the noise doesn’t bother me, doesn’t bother Ayesha,” Curry said in the video, which he captioned “PSA”.

articles.title: Korda seeks LPGA Hall of Fame place and familiar success at The Annika
articles.summary: World No 1 Nelly Korda makes her long-awaited return to competition this week at The Annika, live on Sky Sports Golf, seeking a fourth title at the event which would earn her a spot in the LPGA Hall of Fame.
body: Korda will make her first competitive start on the LPGA Tour since the FM Championship in August, and first appearance since the Solheim Cup in September.
The 28-year-old is already a three-time winner in her six prior starts at The Annika driven by Gainbridge at Pelican Golf Club, and is chasing her fifth win of the season.
"Eight weeks - I don't remember the last time I took that long off," said Korda.
"It was nice but by the middle of it I was ready to get going. There is only so many hours you can go out and practise and beat balls.

articles.title: US withdraw from U-17 World Cup in Qatar due to safety concerns
articles.summary: USSF cites state department advisory about Qatar. Competition set to kick off in eight days. The US men’s national team have pulled out of the Fifa U-17 World Cup, which is due to kick off in Qatar in just over a week.
body: “Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances … we are no longer able to participate in the tournament,” US Soccer’s letter to players reads. “The wellbeing of our players and staff will always be our top priority.
“Please accept our deepest appreciation for your commitment to US Soccer and our shared disappointment about these circumstances.”
A US Soccer spokesperson said the federation would not go into details about how it reached its decision. The Guardian understands Fifa was informed of the federation’s decision on Wednesday.

Fifa’s regulations for the U-17 World Cups stipulate that qualified nations must participate in the tournament or be fined, with withdrawal within 30 days of the tournament’s start resulting in a fine of CHF20,000 (about $24,000). Fifa has been approached for comment.

articles.title: Meeting of two lost souls: can Pochettino make it work at Manchester United? | Barney Ronay
articles.summary: Manager has been hurt by experiences at elite clubs but several players at Old Trafford could fit his playing style. Welcome, Mauricio, to the meat grinder. Or rather, welcome back. We’ve been expecting you.
body: Well, maybe we’re finally here. Maybe he just needed to be broken enough to make it fit. And who knows, perhaps there is even a kind of accidental synergy here.

By now Pochettino has been thoroughly processed through the soul-extraction machinery of elite club football. He arrives at Old Trafford pre-minced, pre‑haunted, a 54-year-old already bruised by his experiences at Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and Levy‑era Spurs. This is a head coach so steeped in the blood of dysfunctional super-clubs that turning back is pretty much the same thing as heading on into its ultimate form in the west end of Manchester.

The problems at Old Trafford are of course unrelated to the appointment of the latest managerial avatar. The constant hiring and firing is a symptom not a cause. This is essentially a distraction, a false flag drawing attention from the avarice and incompetence of the executive tiers.
Still, though, it is necessary on these occasions to set out the reasons why the latest appointment probably won’t work. First up is the obvious sense of diminishing returns.

articles.summary: Mirra Andreeva wins 11 games in a row to thrash world number two Aryna Sabalenka and reach the last four at the WTA Finals.
body: Mirra Andreeva won 11 games in a row as she thrashed world number two Aryna Sabalenka to reach the last four at the WTA Finals.
French Open champion Andreeva was 4-1 down in the opening set before producing some superb tennis and taking advantage of an increasingly erratic Sabalenka performance.
The 19-year-old Russian went on to deliver a statement 6-4 6-0 victory over four-time major singles winner Sabalenka.
"I will be honest, I feel like Aryna did not have the best day," Andreeva told Sky Sports.

articles.title: Youth, intensity, belief: United ready to gamble on Pochettino
articles.summary: With a reputation for developing youth and inspiring players and fans to buy into his brand of high-intensity football, Mauricio Pochettino appears on the cusp of taking the reins at troubled Premier League giants Manchester United.
body: In a move expected to end Pochettino's two-year tenure as USA coach, the Argentine reportedly reached a verbal agreement Wednesday to replace Michael Carrick following United's worst start to a season in 40 years.

United, who have cycled through 11 managers (including caretakers) and failed to win a single league title since Alex Ferguson's 2013 retirement, are desperately in need of a leader who can bring identity, stability and belief to an expensive-but-fragmented squad, and their disillusioned fans.

So the appeal of an inspirational coach who had his Southampton squad walk barefoot across hot coals, took Tottenham Hotspur to a Champions League final, and inspired a nation to believe the US could beat anyone at last summer's World Cup on home soil, is not hard to spot.
Pochettino spoke often before the World Cup of his desire to transform "expectation into energy", and "create amazing energy between the fans and us."

articles.title: Kentucky WBB is on a historic shooting heater after Emily McDonald’s record-breaking night in win vs. Evansville
articles.summary: Kentucky women’s basketball is on a historic shooting heater from deep. If the Wildcats shoot anywhere close to how they have over the last two games, this team will legitimately challenge for a Final Four. We already knew they had the size with three 6-foot-5 starters.
body: And watching this team practice, we knew they had the shooting. It hadn’t shown up until NC State. The Cats were just 24 percent on 3s heading into that game. But these last two games?
Adding this level of record-breaking perimeter firepower makes them a nightmare matchup for anyone in the country.
The Purple Aces were heavily outmatched, and I said beforehand how important it would be to see whether Kentucky could keep its intensity up against a lesser opponent.
They did not play with their food. The Wildcats jumped out to a 21-7 lead in the first quarter, stretched the advantage to 46-11 at halftime, and ultimately cruised to a 98-30 victory.

articles.title: Ex-Ryder Cup Captain Warns Bryson DeChambeau Against ‘Dumb’ YouTube Plan
articles.summary: Former European Ryder Cup captain Paul McGinley has issued a stark warning to Bryson DeChambeau regarding his future in professional golf. The 33-year-old American faces an uncertain path after the collapse of the LIV Golf League.
body: DeChambeau holds a unique spot in the game right now. He won the 2024 U.S. Open at Pinehurst and is eligible for full DP World Tour membership. He may have to wait “at least until next August” to return to PGA under current rules. Rory McIlroy told reporters in Dubai that the American is running out of options if he wants to play competitive golf. The two-time major winner must decide between regular tour play or a content-heavy schedule.

McGinley spoke on the Sky Sports Golf podcast about the risks of a YouTube-only career. He sees a clear path where DeChambeau creates videos while trying to stay sharp for the four majors. McGinley does not think this will work well. “It will be a dumb move. I mean, to go from playing YouTube golf to trying to compete in majors,” he said, according to GolfMagic. The former captain points out that players need to be in the flow of regular tournament golf to win big events. The disconnect from tour play hurts performance over time.

articles.title: Tuchel committed to England - but plotting club return after Three Lions stint
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel revealed he has no release clause in his England contract but is committed to leading them until Euro 2028 at least - even if a big club comes calling.
body: The Three Lions boss was asked the question amid Mauricio Pochettino agreeing a deal in principle with Manchester United to replace Michael Carrick, who is expected to be sacked in the coming days. The USA manager has a £7m buyout clause in his deal.

"No release clause," confirmed Tuchel, who signed his current contract in February. "And there's no intention. I signed the contract - I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business."

Tuchel was then asked if there was "zero chance" he would leave England if a big club came in for him between now and the 2028 Euros, which will be hosted in England. The manager said: "Yeah, I would say so."
Tuchel led England to the semi-finals at this summer's World Cup in the USA, where they were beaten in heartbreaking fashion by Argentina.

articles.title: Shrewsbury 'hit all the boxes' for new owners - Friedel
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with BBC Radio Shropshire new Shrewsbury Town sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is a perfect fit for the new owners.
body: Shrewsbury Town's new sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is the perfect project for the US-backed owners after a Europe-wide search ended with them taking contol of the League Two outfit.

Scott Davidson's Biscayne ST LLC consortium, which Friedel is part of, completed their takeover on Monday, buying 87.4% of the shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to relinquish control.
"Scott and I met through friends in Miami and through the love of football and nothing more or less," former Blackburn and USA goalkeeper Friedel told BBC Radio Shropshire in an exclusive interview.
"As we got to know each other, our thoughts on business and football aligned - we got to the point where we said let's try to find a club which fits a whole bunch of criteria.
